description: We're building an AI-powered health monitoring tool for astronauts using NASA data. Our app will track key vitals, detect anomalies, and show clear dashboards for mission crews. We're looking for a Python/ML developer, a front-end developer, and a data analyst. Beginners with good energy are welcome. Join us and let's build something real in 48 hours!
summary: CosmoCare AI is a web-based health monitoring and decision-support tool that helps astronauts assess their own health on long-duration missions. During a daily check-in, the astronaut enters heart rate, blood pressure, fasting glucose, body temperature, sleep, mood, SpO2 and weight. A FastAPI backend classifies each indicator as green (normal), yellow (caution) or red (alert), computes a 0-100 health score, and returns plain-language guidance. A clickable body map shows the status of six body systems, and every indicator is linked to NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight (space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity, and hostile closed environments). Red alerts prompt the astronaut to contact the flight surgeon. This addresses the challenge by giving crews a clear, visual way to evaluate and act on their health when help from Earth is delayed.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

CosmoCare AI lets an astronaut complete a daily biometric check-in and instantly see how each indicator compares with its reference range. Results are shown as green, yellow or red, with a 0-100 health score, a short explanation of why the indicator matters in spaceflight, and a recommended action. If any indicator is red, the app tells the astronaut to contact the flight surgeon.

HOW IT WORKS

- Frontend (Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS): check-in form with Healthy, Stressed and Critical presets, results panel, clickable body map (six systems: nervous, cardiovascular, respiratory, musculoskeletal, immune, metabolic), trend analytics, mental wellbeing check-in, health assistant and printable reports.

- Backend (Python, FastAPI, Pydantic): POST /api/checkin validates the inputs and applies reference ranges for heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, glucose, temperature, sleep and mood. Each indicator is tagged with the related NASA hazards, a body part, an explanation and guidance. SpO2 and weight are recorded in the interface but are not scored by the backend yet.

- The backend also includes a z-score anomaly detection module that runs on simulated crew telemetry (personal baseline vs recent readings).

- ML component (folder ml/): a simulated 14-day dataset for four astronauts, personal-baseline deviation and trend analysis, and plots for sleep, mood and heart rate. It flags gradual declines (for example in sleep and mood). It is included in the repository and is not yet integrated into the live dashboard.

BENEFITS

Astronauts on long missions carry much of the responsibility for spotting health changes in themselves. CosmoCare AI explains measurements, shows risks at a glance with color coding, and links each result to the spaceflight hazard behind it, so users do not need prior medical knowledge.

LIMITS

All data is simulated. This is a demo tool, not a medical device, and it does not replace flight surgeon guidance. Reference ranges are general adult values, and the caution and alert cut-offs and score penalties are project-defined for demonstration.

TOOLS

Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, GitHub and Vercel.

CODE: https://github.com/Huzaifaahmedbhutto/cosmocare-ai

LIVE APP: https://cosmocare-ai-werj.vercel.app

LIVE API DOCS: https://cosmocare-ai.vercel.app/docs

USE OF AI (SUPER INTELLIGENCE) TOOLS

- Code: AI assistants helped write and debug parts of the code. Claude (Anthropic): FastAPI backend (check-in rules and endpoints), first version of the Next.js check-in page, deployment steps and documentation drafts. Google AI Studio and an AI chat assistant: frontend dashboard interface. ChatGPT (OpenAI): ML scripts and the simulated dataset in the ml/ folder.

- Images and design: Gemini / NotebookLM were used to help create the demo slide deck (design and visuals). Any AI-generated images in the deck are credited to AI tools here and on slide 6 of the deck.

- Data: all health data in the demo is simulated and was generated by our own scripts.

The team reviewed, tested and integrated all AI-assisted outputs. No NASA logos, flags or mission identifiers were used.
